extracted.intended_audience: explorers, surveyors, and general readers of 19th-century travel/exploration narratives
extracted.subtask_description: Practical field reporting and narrative of coastal/river exploration: surveying harbours, interacting with Indigenous peoples, recording natural history, and documenting navigational and geological data. Emphasises accurate observation, specimen collection, and caution in ethnolinguistic recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for procuring water in the bush
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical techniques for obtaining water when travelling in arid or unfamiliar country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect dew from leaves with a sponge (sometimes yields up to a pint); dig up lateral roots of small gumtrees, break them into short bits and set them to drain into bark or a shell; tap knotty excrescences of trees and suck out the fluid. Note that natives also use these methods and that some techniques are dusty and fatiguing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveying harbours and inlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically trace branches and openings of a harbour to determine navigable extents and obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put surveying force to instant requisition; explore openings with boats, trace branches in compass directions and measure distances navigable (e.g., 'traced ten miles in a south-easterly direction'); note where navigation is blocked by large blocks of granite or mangrove networks and record the furthest points boats can advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wildlife and vegetation as indicators of freshwater
rubrics_metrics.description: Infer the presence of fresh water and swamps from local fauna and flora observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe bird movements (e.g., flocks of white ibises flying from the south indicating a swamp); note green appearance of gumtrees and clumps of palms which often mark fresh water nearby; look for driftwood and trees deposited by overflows as evidence of water flow from inland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise coordinates, soundings, and geological strata
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide exact positional data and physical descriptions for wells, islands, headlands, and geological strata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give latitude and longitude for noteworthy features (e.g., position of a well); record depth soundings and tidal depths in fathoms; describe strata composition and depths (ironstone mixed with marl, sandstone in decomposition, sandy mud) and note where water oozes in wells and at what depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming discoveries and features
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign names to newly noted geographic features often commemorating people, events, or striking physical resemblance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include naming points after officers who found water (Point Emery), naming harbours after persons (Bynoe Harbour), or naming ranges after notable likenesses (McAdam Range). Explain reasoning where appropriate (e.g., 'in honour of Mr. McAdam').

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging with indigenous peoples—behavioural caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach interactions with Indigenous people with cautious respect and awareness of their likely fears and customs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume absence of visible weapons means they are unarmed—their arms may be nearby or concealed; recognise fear responses (e.g., at cigars/fire) and be patient until fear subsides; avoid forcing them on board; observe maternal/child behaviour and respect it; be aware that theatrical grimaces or gestures may signal terror, not hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting accurate vocabularies from Indigenous speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and cautions for compiling word-lists from transient contacts with native speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a vocabulary only of words 'we know to be correct'; compare words among multiple collectors and across visits; beware that many recorded words may actually mean 'What do you mean?' or 'I do not understand' rather than object names; account for dialect variation and the fact that transient visitors often cannot obtain a correct vocabulary; repeated verification over time is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigation and anchorage markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and record practical markers and guidance for safe anchoring and passage through channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify best anchorage (e.g., 'near Point Emery'); note visual leading marks (e.g., 'the extreme of the latter, and a clump of peaked bushes...make a good mark for leading out'); warn of drying patches and sandbanks and give bearings to avoid them; advise on channel choices and when to haul towards islands to avoid hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tidal measurement and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report tidal behaviour at explored ports and inlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record tidal range at springs and neaps (e.g., rise at springs 24 feet, at neaps sometimes only two); note tidal rate in knots and the time of high water at full and change of the moon; observe irregularities and record flood/ebb directions to inform navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey technique for shallow-water navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical approach for finding a channel for a larger vessel using smaller craft and soundings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use boats ahead to 'feel our way' with soundings, anchor when depths are insufficient for the ship, and send parties to examine openings; locate channels of sufficient depth (six, seven, ten fathoms) near islands and between ledges before attempting to bring the ship through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting natural phenomena and weather
rubrics_metrics.description: Record unusual celestial or meteorological events and anomalies encountered during the voyage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report observations such as brilliant meteors (with direction, angle, duration), unexpected squalls out of season (time and severity), and temperature changes (maxima and minima) as they may be noteworthy for future navigators and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting natural-history specimens and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather specimens of flora and fauna and create illustrations or appendices for scientific and public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make seine hauls and collect rare/curious fish and bird specimens; add coloured drawings or specimens to appendices and collections; record locations where specimens were taken and any unusual distributional notes (e.g., a bird being the farthest south observed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field safety and contingency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare for and respond to immediate physical dangers and sudden weather changes during exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to hazards such as alligators when wading or swimming—avoid isolating oneself far from the boat; carry appropriate gear (anchors—use a second anchor in severe squalls); be ready to anchor overnight when forced by tide/wind; preserve weapons and equipment when retreat is necessary.
